// diagnostic E3218

Jet.CallbackReadsContext

The C callback {callback} reads `context.{member}`.

What

The C callback {callback} reads `context.{member}`.

Why

C calls a callback on a thread it chooses, where no Jet task runs, so there is no task context to read.

Fix

Read the value before the foreign call and pass it to the callback through C, or drop the read.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning Jet.CallbackReadsContext: Tests/UI/Cffi/ManagedCallbackSafety/stderr.

Error: Jet.CallbackReadsContext: The C callback lambda reads `context.thread`.
  --> Tests/UI/Cffi/ManagedCallbackSafety/run.jet:4:20
    |
  4 |     source.on_data(fn(event) {
    |                    ^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: C calls a callback on a thread it chooses, where no Jet task runs, so there is no task context to read.
 Fix: Read the value before the foreign call and pass it to the callback through C, or drop the read.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/Jet.CallbackReadsContext

Error: Jet.ValueNotSendable: `cell` can't be captured by a foreign C callback because `Cell<Int>` isn't sendable
  --> Tests/UI/Cffi/ManagedCallbackSafety/run.jet:11:20
    |
 11 |     source.on_data(fn(event) {
    |                    ^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: Foreign C callbacks are retained by C and invoked on a thread C chooses, so their captured state must be owned and thread-safe
 Fix: Capture only owned sendable values in the foreign callback, or use `Shared<T>` for synchronized state
More: jet-lang.dev/e/Jet.ValueNotSendable

Error: Jet.ConcurrentCaptureNotOwned: `count` cannot cross the `foreign C callback` boundary: the value writes shared state
  --> Tests/UI/Cffi/ManagedCallbackSafety/run.jet:19:20
    |
 19 |     source.on_data(fn(event) {
    |                    ^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: The `foreign C callback` boundary can run concurrently with its owner; the write would race with the owner or require a hidden merge rule
 Fix: Give it away with `.move()`, freeze it with `freeze`, or share it with `Shared{…}`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/Jet.ConcurrentCaptureNotOwned
